Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system

Class NetworkService

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService
public final class NetworkService extends Object
Network-manager abstraction for the LFS/BLFS system managers: it detects which network backend the running system uses (NetworkManager, dhcpcd, systemd-networkd, or a read-only ip fallback) and maps a logical connection/link operation onto that backend's native command line.

This is a thin front-end helper, normative in system-management-contract.md §4.4. It never re-implements networking logic: buildCommand(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Backend, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Operation, java.lang.String) only produces an argument vector (no shell interpolation) that the caller runs through ProcessRunner (read-only operations, always unprivileged) or PrivilegedRunner (mutating operations on dhcpcd/networkd, escalated with polkit). The detection order mirrors the contract exactly: NetworkManager (nmcli or NetworkManager present) → dhcpcd (dhcpcd present) → systemd-networkd (networkctl present) → read-only ip.

NetworkManager is special-cased for privileges: nmcli talks to the NetworkManager daemon over D-Bus and the daemon mediates its own polkit prompt, so runMutating(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Backend, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Operation, java.lang.String) runs nmcli unprivileged and lets NM raise the single prompt (contract §7 item 5, "exactly one polkit prompt"). dhcpcd/networkd have no such broker, so their mutating verbs are escalated here via PrivilegedRunner.

The detection, command-building and parsing logic is pure and unit-testable (detect(Probes), buildCommand(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Backend, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Operation, java.lang.String), parseInterfaces(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Backend, java.lang.String)); the live detect() probe and the run*/list* helpers are thin wrappers that degrade gracefully (an unknown backend or an unsupported operation yields an empty vector rather than throwing).

  • Method Details

    • detect

      public static NetworkService.Backend detect(NetworkService.Probes p)
      Pure detection from a set of probes, in the contract's §4.4 order: NetworkManager (either nmcli or the NetworkManager daemon binary), then dhcpcd, then systemd-networkd, then a read-only ip fallback. Returns NetworkService.Backend.NONE only when even ip is absent (nothing to show).

    • detect

      public static NetworkService.Backend detect()
      Live detection against this host: probes PATH for each backend tool, then defers to detect(Probes).

    • isMutating

      public static boolean isMutating(NetworkService.Operation op)
      True if op changes system state (brings a link up/down).

    • isSupported

      public static boolean isSupported(NetworkService.Backend backend, NetworkService.Operation op)
      True if backend supports op. NetworkService.Backend.NONE supports nothing; the read-only NetworkService.Backend.IP fallback supports the read verbs but never a mutating one.

    • requiresTarget

      public static boolean requiresTarget(NetworkService.Backend backend, NetworkService.Operation op)
      True if op needs an interface/connection target on backend. NetworkService.Operation.LIST never does; NetworkService.Operation.STATUS does for every backend except NetworkManager (nmcli device status reports all devices at once); up/down always do.

    • needsPrivileges

      public static boolean needsPrivileges(NetworkService.Backend backend, NetworkService.Operation op)
      True if a mutating op on backend must be escalated with polkit here. Only dhcpcd/networkd do: NetworkManager mediates its own prompt over D-Bus, so nmcli runs unprivileged.

    • buildCommand

      public static List<String> buildCommand(NetworkService.Backend backend, NetworkService.Operation op, String target)
      Builds the argument vector for op on backend, targeting target (an interface or connection name). Returns an empty list when the operation is unsupported or a required target is missing; the result never contains shell metacharacters and is meant to be handed straight to ProcessRunner / PrivilegedRunner.

      dhcpcd's NetworkService.Operation.LIST is file-based: the contract sources the interface list from /etc/dhcpcd.conf (a read-only state file, §3.5) rather than a CLI, so this returns an empty vector for that one case and listInterfaces(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.NetworkService.Backend) reads the config instead.

    • runRead

      public static ProcessRunner.Result runRead(NetworkService.Backend backend, NetworkService.Operation op, String target)
      Runs a read-only operation (LIST or STATUS) unprivileged through ProcessRunner (contract §4.4: "MUST run read-only probes unprivileged"). Returns a not-started ProcessRunner.Result when the operation is unsupported or mutating.

    • runMutating

      public static PrivilegedRunner.PrivilegedResult runMutating(NetworkService.Backend backend, NetworkService.Operation op, String target)
      Runs a mutating operation (UP/DOWN). On dhcpcd/networkd it is escalated with polkit through PrivilegedRunner; on NetworkManager it runs nmcli unprivileged and lets the daemon raise its own single prompt. Returns an ERROR result when the operation is unsupported or read-only.

    • listInterfaces

      public static List<NetworkService.NetInterface> listInterfaces(NetworkService.Backend backend)
      Lists the connections/links for backend, read-only and unprivileged. For NetworkManager/networkd/ip this runs the LIST command and parses its stdout; for dhcpcd it reads /etc/dhcpcd.conf (a read-only state file). Returns an empty list when the backend is NetworkService.Backend.NONE, absent or errors.

    • readDhcpcdConf

      public static String readDhcpcdConf()
      Reads /etc/dhcpcd.conf read-only; "" when unreadable.

    • parseInterfaces

      public static List<NetworkService.NetInterface> parseInterfaces(NetworkService.Backend backend, String out)
      Parses a backend's NetworkService.Operation.LIST output into NetworkService.NetInterface values. The exact shape differs by backend:
      • NetworkManager nmcli -t -f NAME,TYPE,DEVICE connection show: one colon-separated connection per line (the device field is empty for an inactive connection).
      • networkd networkctl list: a columnar table with an IDX LINK TYPE OPERATIONAL SETUP header and an N links listed. footer, both skipped.
      • ip ip -o link show: N: name[@if]: <FLAGS> ... state S ..., one link per line.
      • dhcpcd: out is the text of /etc/dhcpcd.conf; the interface / allowinterfaces names are extracted.
      Blank and malformed lines are skipped; parsing never throws.
